# Crisp

> Crisp (also called Crisp Video, or Crisp for Mac) restores, denoises and
> upscales old, low-res video to 4K offline on your Mac, with a real timeline
> editor. Free with a small "Made with Crisp" mark on exports; Pro is $129
> once, with no subscription. Your photos and videos are processed entirely on
> your Mac: no uploads, no analytics, no telemetry.

Crisp needs macOS 26 (Tahoe) or later on Apple Silicon. One licence covers up
to 3 Macs at a time; deactivate one to move it to another. Refunds: 30 days,
no reason needed.

What it cannot do: nothing recovers the original detail, because it was never
recorded. What AI upscaling adds is plausible detail, not the original's; the
Learn pages explain what it can and cannot fix.

## Get Crisp

- [Download Crisp for Mac](https://crispvideo.app/download/): Free to use, with a small "Made with Crisp" mark on exports; Pro is $129 once. Needs macOS 26 (Tahoe) or later on Apple Silicon.
- [Pricing](https://crispvideo.app/#pricing): Free, or Pro for $129 once.
- [Refund policy](https://crispvideo.app/legal/refunds/): 30-day refunds, no reason needed. How to request one, and your statutory rights in the UK and EU.

- [The best Mac video tools, compared](https://crispvideo.app/best/): Roundups of the best video upscalers, compressors, converters, denoisers and stabilizers for Mac, including the free ones.
- [Who uses Crisp](https://crispvideo.app/for/): How Crisp is used by wedding videographers, family archivists, YouTubers, teachers, churches and others, with the settings each one tends to need.
- [Learn: video restoration explained](https://crispvideo.app/learn/): Plain-English explainers on the video terms that decide how your footage turns out, including what AI upscaling can and cannot fix.
